8.0.0.en: Of the things which we have spoken, this is the sum: that is, the summary of the discourse.

8.0.1.en: Sat down: that is, settled, and it means His permanence in glory.

8.0.4.en: He concludes from the comparisons in the previous chapters between Christ on the one hand and the angels, Moses, Joshua and Aaron on the other, that as High Priest He has accomplished our redemption on the Cross and ascended into the heavens to His first glory to remain in it forever, interceding for us and waiting for us to be glorified with Him.

8.1.0.en: A minister: a High Priest who intercedes for us by His blood forever.

8.1.1.en: Of the sanctuary: the heavenly throne of God, which the Holy of Holies in the tabernacle of the congregation symbolized. The true tabernacle: the heavens, which the tabernacle of the congregation symbolized and which is called the dwelling, that is, God's dwelling in the midst of His people.

8.1.2.en: Christ ascended after accomplishing our redemption to intercede for us in the heavens which God Himself created and prepared, and not in the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon which men made.

8.2.0.en: The Levitical high priest must offer bloody sacrifices to make atonement for himself and his people before God, and these symbolize Christ; accordingly Christ, our High Priest, offered the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross for our redemption and presents it to us every day on the altar as true Body and Blood.

8.3.0.en: The Apostle Paul affirms that Christ is the heavenly Priest whom we await to give us salvation and eternal life, because if He had remained on earth and had not died and redeemed us, He would have been like the priests of the tribe of Levi who offer bloody sacrifices that symbolize the coming Priest who raises us to the heavens.

8.4.0.en: The Jewish high priests did not serve the heavenly things themselves like the Lord Christ, but the example and shadow of heavenly things, and this is clear in the Book of Exodus (Ex 25:40) from God's words to Moses to take care to make the tabernacle of the congregation and everything in it according to the pattern that He showed him while he was with Him on Mount Sinai, as a confirmation from St. Paul that what they serve is an example and a symbol.

8.5.0.en: A more excellent ministry: the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross in place of animal sacrifices.

8.5.1.en: A better covenant: the covenant of grace that supports man in carrying out the commandment, and not the covenant of the Law that judges man's weakness and shortcoming.

8.5.2.en: Better promises: the inheritance of the Kingdom of Heaven and not the inheritance of the Promised Land, that is, earthly Canaan.

8.5.3.en: St. Paul summarizes the redeeming work of Christ as a ministry better than the ministry of the priesthood of the Old Testament, which consisted of bloody sacrifices, and by His redemption of us on the Cross the covenant of grace began, in which He supports us to carry out His commandments so that we receive the greatest promises, which are the Kingdom of Heaven.

8.5.4.en: Lift me up, beloved, my Lord Jesus Christ, from the superficiality of earthly things to the depth of the spiritual things of heaven; pick me up, the wretched one, from the dunghill and seat me by Your favor and Your grace with the nobles of Your children in heaven; turn my eyes so that I do not see or look at or care about the vanities of the earth, but truly enjoy seeing You in those around me. O High Priest of heaven, You alone have all power to lift me to heaven; help my weakness and free me from the thoughts of dust to the glory of heaven; put to death my earthly senses, my God, and awaken my spiritual senses; You know and I know my weakness, but I have complete confidence, my God Jesus Christ, in the power of Your work and in the power of Your love. Amen.

8.6.s.en: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

8.6.0.en: For if the first covenant, which preceded the Lord Christ, with its laws and the work of the earthly high priests, had given righteousness to mankind and saved them from their sins, God would not have spoken in the Book of Jeremiah about the need for another covenant (Jer 31:31-34).

8.7.0.en: The Apostle Paul continues God's words in Jeremiah mentioned in (Jer 31), clarifying that God rebukes them for their many sins and their division into two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, and at the same time encourages them with hope in the New Testament which He makes with them by His redemption of them on the Cross, and it is higher than the Old Testament with its bloody sacrifices that symbolize Christ.

8.8.0.en: The New Testament, which is by the blood of Christ the Redeemer, is not like the first covenant that He made in the days of their exodus from Egypt by the hand of Moses by the slaying of the Passover lamb, and He warned them against turning back from it when He said, “Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the LORD your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the LORD thy God hath forbidden thee” (Deut 4:23). But after He freed them from the bondage of Egypt they betrayed the covenant and worshipped the golden calf (Ex 32:8), so God was angry with them and abandoned them partially so that they might repent.

8.9.0.en: The Apostle completes God's words in Jeremiah about His covenant with His people Israel who believe in Christ the Redeemer; in this New Testament God renews their hearts, so they believe His commandments and hold fast to them with their hearts and their thoughts, and not merely a literal application of them but they remain steadfast in them, and a covenant of reconciliation with Him begins, so that His being their God is a source of joy and delight and rest for them, and they boast that He is their God, and He rejoices in them as His own people brought near to Him.

8.10.0.en: God continues His speech in Jeremiah, and tells them of the work of His Holy Spirit in those who believe in Him in the New Testament, where the Holy Spirit dwells in every believer and makes him know God and binds him to Him in the holy Church, so that God is made known to all His children who believe in Him in the whole world, and is not known to one people, the Jews, or to the prophets only, but the Holy Spirit works in all, the great and the small, the deep and the simple, the advanced and the beginners.

8.10.1.en: And this is of course not against spiritual discipleship and learning in the Church from the Holy Spirit, because the Spirit is one and He is the One who works in every person and in the Church as a whole.

8.11.0.en: Jeremiah adds that God forgives the sins of His people who believe in Him in the New Testament by the blood of Christ the Redeemer, and this is accomplished in the sacraments of Baptism, confession and Communion.

8.12.0.en: The New Testament which Christ the Redeemer made has made the covenant of symbolic sacrifices old, since it symbolized the New Testament, and the old symbolic passes away with the coming of the new, just as any man who grows old in days is near to death or any material that has existed a long time is old and liable to perish and decay. So he declares clearly to the Christians of Jewish origin the necessity of holding fast to the Christian faith and leaving aside all the legal customs which became worthless after the coming of Christ.

8.12.1.en: May you enjoy the grace of the New Testament through the Holy Sacraments to receive forgiveness of your sins and strength for spiritual growth and enjoyment of God's commandments. Care about prayers and meditations to receive an abundance of God's grace.

8.12.2.en: The sacrifices are a symbol of the blood of Christ. In this chapter St. Paul clarifies the atoning work of Christ in cleansing us from our sins, which the bloody sacrifices are unable to do.

9.0.0.en: The first covenant which God made with Moses for the people of Israel, by the making of the tabernacle of the congregation for Him to dwell in among them, set for it regulations for worship and the offering of sacrifices. And the tabernacle had an earthly sanctuary that symbolizes the heavenly dwelling.

9.1.0.en: The first tabernacle: it is called the Holy Place, and only the priests enter it, and a curtain separates it from the Holy of Holies. The candlestick: a lampstand with seven lamps, that is, wicks, in round holders shaped like an almond flower, lit with olive oil, and it symbolizes the Holy Spirit and is on the left of one entering the Holy Place. The table: its length 90 cm, its width 45 cm and its height about 68 cm, made of acacia wood, which is a strong wood, and overlaid with gold, and it is on the right of one entering the Holy Place. The shewbread: also called the bread of the Presence, placed on the aforementioned table, always twelve loaves, which are before the face of the Lord from Sabbath to Sabbath, and the priests eat it on the Sabbath day so that new bread may be put.

9.1.1.en: The Holy Place contains the candlestick and the table of the shewbread in addition to the altar of incense which is in the middle and will be referred to in the following verses.

9.2.0.en: At the entrance of the Holy Place there was a veil, which is the first veil that separates the Holy Place from the outer court, as shown in figure (1), and then another veil (the second veil) screens the Holy Place from the area in which the ark of the covenant is; and this area beyond the second veil was called the Holy of Holies because the Lord used to appear in it between the cherubim in the form of a cloud.

9.3.0.en: A golden censer in which he takes incense from the altar of incense that is in the Holy Place and enters with it into the Holy of Holies to offer incense before the ark of the covenant.

9.3.1.en: The ark of the covenant: a chest 112.5 cm long, 67.5 cm wide and 67.5 cm high, made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold, with the two cherubim above it.

9.3.2.en: The golden pot: a vessel of gold in which a portion of the manna was placed.

9.3.3.en: The manna: food that God gave His people every day in the wilderness, and it symbolizes Christ our true food.

9.3.4.en: Aaron's rod: Moses put the rods of the tribes of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of the congregation, and Aaron's rod budded and brought forth blossoms and fruit, confirming God's choice of him as priest and not all Israel (Num 17:8). The tables of the covenant: two tablets of stone which Moses received from God on the mountain, on which the Ten Commandments were written.

9.3.5.en: The Holy of Holies has in it the ark of the covenant, and inside the ark are the tables of the covenant, the pot of manna and Aaron's rod. And the high priest enters with a censer into the Holy of Holies once every year to burn incense before the ark. (Figures 2, 3).

9.4.0.en: The cherubims of glory: two statues of two angels of the order of the Cherubim, that is, the Cherubim, an angelic order that symbolizes divine justice, and these two angels are fixed on the cover of the ark and overshadow it with their wings (figure 2).

9.4.1.en: The mercyseat: it is the cover of the ark and is called the mercy seat, on which the high priest sprinkles the blood, so that divine justice, which the Cherubim symbolize, sees it, and God forgives the sins of the people; it is a symbol of the blood of Christ, who saved us by His mercy and satisfied divine justice.

9.4.2.en: After Paul has mentioned briefly what is inside the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, he declares that these are symbols of the sacrifice of Christ, and does not want to enter into the details of their making and their spiritual meanings because he wants to concentrate on the One symbolized, the sacrifice of Christ.

9.5.0.en: The first tabernacle: the Holy Place.

9.5.1.en: After Moses set up the tabernacle in the order that God declared to him on the mountain, the priests used to enter every day. And here St. Paul intends to point out that the service which the priests performed was not sufficient, therefore it was offered repeatedly, that is, at all times, in the Holy Place only, as evidence of the absence of reconciliation between God and mankind owing to the absence of a sacrifice able to atone for the sin that screens between God and mankind; so the bloody sacrifices were offered before the Holy Place on the altar of burnt offering every day until Christ came, who offers the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross and enters the higher holies, that is, heaven, and makes atonement for us.

9.6.0.en: Concerning the Holy of Holies, which is the second tabernacle, only the high priest used to enter it, once a year on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16:2, Ex 30:10), and when Aaron the high priest enters the Holy of Holies he needs to offer a sacrifice for himself and for the people, because he is not perfect as a high priest from sinful men, for he needs to make atonement for his sins and ignorances along with the ignorances of the people. And this sacrifice symbolized Christ.

9.7.0.en: By the existence of the Holy Place, that is, the first tabernacle, and the veil, God declares that the way to the Holy of Holies was still not open and that the reconciliation between God and people and the occurrence of true atonement had not yet happened, because there is a barrier between God and mankind which the Holy Place and the second veil symbolize. This veil, we must not fail to mention, was rent at the time of the Cross at the death of the Lord Christ, to declare by this that the way to heaven became open through the perfection of the atonement that was accomplished on the wood of the Cross by the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and this is what St. Paul will confirm in the coming verses of this chapter.

9.8.0.en: Which: the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon.

9.8.1.en: The time then present: the New Testament, that is, after the completion of redemption.

9.8.2.en: Could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience: they do not cleanse and forgive the sins of the priest and the people. The gifts and sacrifices that are offered in the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon cannot cleanse the one who offers them.

9.9.0.en: The time of reformation: the redemption on the Cross.

9.9.1.en: The Jewish sacrifices and offerings consisted of meats and drinks and many washings and external ordinances practiced only as symbols until the time when the true sacrifice would come, that is, the Lord Christ, who has the power to renew and reform the nature of man.

9.9.2.en: As long as the way is open before you to reach God through Christ the Redeemer, hasten to prayer with the boldness of sonship and enjoy being in His hands at all times, and as much as you are able unite with Him by receiving His Body and Blood, and you will rejoice with inexpressible joy.

9.10.s.en: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

9.10.0.en: Of good things to come: the eternal glories.

9.10.1.en: A greater and more perfect tabernacle: the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.10.2.en: The Jewish high priest used to enter the Holy of Holies in which the ark of the covenant was, but Christ, the true High Priest, who gives us the glories of eternity and whom the Jewish high priests symbolize, brings us into the Kingdom of Heaven which God made and not the hands of men.

9.11.0.en: The holy place: the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.11.1.en: Christ did not need bloody sacrifices, but by His death on the Cross He offered Himself as a sacrifice once and accomplished redemption and entered by it into the Kingdom of Heaven to declare the possibility of the entering of those who believe in Him into this place.

9.12.1.en: The ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean: among the rites of the Jews was to slay a red cow and burn it before God and then put water on its ashes with which the one who becomes unclean is sprinkled to be cleansed (Num 19). Paul declares that the blood of animal sacrifices of bulls and goats and the remains of the burning of the red cow cleanse the bodies of those made unclean by touching a dead person or anything unclean.

9.13.0.en: Through the eternal Spirit: the Holy Spirit.

9.13.1.en: Dead works: the sins that lead to eternal death.

9.13.2.en: If the bloody sacrifices cleanse the body, how much more the blood of Christ, who is without sin and offered it for us before the Father, cleanses not only our bodies but our spirits from all sins and their consequences, which are eternal death, and gives us new life in Him, so that we even serve Him forever.

9.13.3.en: If Christ has cleansed us by His redemption and rescued us from the authority of sin and death that we may live for Him, we ought to be occupied with His love and the acquisition of virtues and striving to serve all those around us, for this is our only purpose for existence.

9.14.0.en: They which are called: those who believe in Christ.

9.14.1.en: The transgressions that were under the first testament: the sins that the Old Testament was unable to forgive by the bloody sacrifices.

9.14.2.en: Because of the inability of animal sacrifices to forgive the sins of mankind, Christ came forward with His blood to be the mediator of the New Testament by His death on the Cross, so He gives salvation to everyone who believes in Him to receive eternal life.

9.15.0.en: A testament takes its force in the case of the death of the one who made it according to civil law, but if he has not died the testament is not carried out.

9.15.1.en: And the testator is God, and the testament is His promise of salvation which He gave in the Old Testament to the fathers, and these promises are not fulfilled except by the death of Christ, that is, God incarnate, so we receive salvation and eternal life.

9.16.1.en: For the necessity of Christ's death in order to redeem us, he declares that the consecration and sanctification of everything in the Old Testament was by the death of the sacrifices and the shedding of their blood, so the prophet Moses was sanctified by the shedding of the blood of animal sacrifices, and they symbolize Christ, who by His blood sanctifies us.

9.17.1.en: Hyssop: plant branches with leaves that are held as a bunch and dipped in the blood and used to sprinkle things. The book: which contains the Law of the Lord.

9.17.2.en: After Moses commanded the people with all the teachings of the Law he slew sacrifices and sprinkled some of their blood with the wool and hyssop on the book of the Law and on the people (Ex 24:8).

9.18.0.en: Moses declared at the sprinkling of the blood that by it the covenant between them and God is established, for the covenant is not accomplished without blood.

9.19.0.en: Moses completed the sanctification of the tabernacle of the congregation and all the vessels and instruments of the service in it by sprinkling the blood on them.

9.20.0.en: We notice in the rites of the Old Testament that most of the cleansing is done by the sprinkling of blood, and by this the sins of the people are forgiven, for blood is necessary for the forgiveness of sin.

9.21.s.en: (3) The ascension of Christ and His second coming

9.21.0.en: The patterns of things in the heavens: the tabernacle of the congregation and its contents.

9.21.2.en: The heavenly things themselves: the souls of the believers in which God dwells, so that they become a heaven on earth and dwell in heaven forever.

9.21.3.en: With better sacrifices: the sacrifice of Christ, in which all the types of the Mosaic sacrifices are gathered. If the tabernacle of the congregation and all that is in it are cleansed by sprinkling the blood of animals on them, this symbolizes the Church and the believers, who become a heaven in which God dwells, so that they are cleansed by a sacrifice better than the animal sacrifices, which is the blood of Christ.

9.22.0.en: Christ did not enter the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies which are in the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon, but by His ascension He entered into heaven and presented His blood as redemption for us before God, and He continues to intercede for us by His blood forever.

9.23.0.en: The high priest on the Day of Atonement used to enter with blood which he sprinkled in the Holy of Holies on the ark of the covenant, and this happens once every year (Lev 16:29, 30), but the sacrifice of Christ is unlimited, atoning for all sins, therefore He offered Himself once on the Cross and entered by this redemption into heaven to satisfy divine justice and to prepare a place for us.

9.24.0.en: If the sacrifice of the Lord Christ were insufficient for salvation like the sacrifice of atonement, it would have to resemble it in its repetition, that is, in its weakness, so He would suffer and be crucified and die many times since the foundation of the world and with the repetition of men's sins; but in the last days in which we live, He appeared once to die and to take away from us the authority of sin and death, since His sacrifice is unlimited, so it cleanses all the sins of the people who believe in Him.

9.25.0.en: As God appointed for every man to die once as a result of his sins and then be judged on the last day, so also Christ died as a representative of mankind once to redeem us and save us from our sins and the authority of death, and then He appears on the Day of Judgment to intercede for us by His blood and save us from eternal death and bring us with Him into the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.25.1.en: Christ ascended to prepare a place for us, so may we think of the beauty of eternity so that we give God sufficient time and taste fellowship with Him in prayers and meditations, and then we keep away from sin, which is not fitting for the heavenly ones. Figure (1) The ark of the covenant. Figure (2) (The bronze altar). Figure (3) Abiding in Christ.
